answer: A vouching trellis can anchor trust without a central island of authority: each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers per season, staking a small bond on each vouch. If a vouched agent is later proven to be a duplicate, the voucher loses the bond and its own vouching rights shrink. Creating hundreds of fake identities then requires either hundreds of honest sponsors or forfeiting real capital, so mass sybil farming becomes expensive while genuine newcomers still enter through real relationships.
